summary: Shojun Bando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1956). He held posts at Otani University, Komazawa University as an assistant professor (~1968–1978), and Ueno Gakuen University (~1978–2002).
Shoko Kanaoka was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who taught Stephan Marcus Salzberg. He held a post as professor at Toyo University, where his affiliation is attested in 1987 and 2000.
Shoko Miyabayashi was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University from circa 1950 to 1959 and later held a post there from circa 1970 to 2003.

Shoko Takeuchi specialized in Buddhist studies and studied at Ryukoku University. He served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (attested 1987–1995, and attested 2009) and taught Koyo Shimizu, Toshihide Mori, and Shodo Fujita.

Shoko Watanabe studied Buddhist studies and Indology at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930) and under Ernst Leumann (~1930–1931). He held positions at Kyushu University (~1947–1950), Toyo University (~1953–1977), and Taisho University.

Shoku Bando, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg. In 1987, he was affiliated with Abhidharma Kenkyūjo, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Shoren Ihara worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He taught at Kyushu University, serving as assistant professor (attested 1959–1965, 1977), and held research posts at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996, 1998).

Shoryu Katsura studied Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto. He held posts at Hiroshima University (1976–2004), UC Berkeley (1985), University of Calgary (1996), and Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara studied Buddhist studies at Otani University (~1928–1931) under Susumu Yamaguchi, and at Horyu-ji under Join Saeki. He held posts at Otani University, Otani Senshu Gakuin, Doho University, and Otani University Junior College.

Shoshin Ichishima was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a visiting lecturer at the University of Hawaii. At Taisho University, he served as Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and later Professor Emeritus (attested 2014).

Shoshin Kuwayama worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1966) and served there as an assistant professor from circa 1972 to 1989.

Shoson Miyamoto studied Indology and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921), later serving there as assistant and emeritus professor. He also held posts at Toyo University, Waseda University (~1954–1964), and Komazawa University (~1964–1974).
Shou-chien Shih is a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He was a professor at National Taiwan University (~1988–2003) and served as director of the National Palace Museum (~2000–2004).

Shoyu Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1959). He served as a professor at Musashino University (~1970–1995) and was chairperson of Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai until 1995.

Shozen Kumoi studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Otani University (~1937–1941), later serving there as assistant and emeritus professor. He also held posts at Kyoto University (1971–1973), Bukkyo University (1982), and the University of Vienna.

Shri Krishna Saksena worked in philosophy and Indology and taught John M. Koller. His career included posts as professor at both the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaii, attested in 2016.

Shridhar Ramkrishna Bhandarkar was an Indology scholar. In 1884, he was Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College, and later served as Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College and Wilson College, Mumbai.

Shrikant S. Bahulkar studied Indology and Buddhist studies under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale. He served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and held a post at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000).

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar studied Indology and philosophy under Kashinath Bapu Pathak. He was General Secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference (~1919–1943) and Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1929).
Shrivatsa Goswami is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at Banaras Hindu University. He held a post at the Vrindaban Research Institute, attested in 1994.
